name: Dock appears instantly
summary: The hidden Dock shows as soon as the pointer reaches the screen edge, with no slide.
benefit: The Dock is there the moment the pointer reaches the edge, instead of after about half a second.
tradeoff: No slide animation, and the Dock can appear when the pointer only brushes the edge.

name: Recent apps in the Dock: off
summary: Removes the Dock section that lists recently used apps.
benefit: A shorter Dock whose icons stay where you put them.
tradeoff: You lose the shortcut back to an app you recently quit.

name: Dock icon bounce at launch: off
summary: App icons no longer bounce in the Dock while the app opens.
benefit: Less movement in the Dock while apps start.
tradeoff: No visual sign that an app is still starting, apart from the indicator dot.

name: Minimize effect: Scale
summary: Windows shrink straight into the Dock instead of using the Genie effect.
benefit: Minimizing looks quicker and simpler.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Keep Spaces in a fixed order
summary: Mission Control stops reordering your desktops by most recent use.
benefit: Each desktop stays in the same position, so Control-number and Control-arrow always reach the same Space.
tradeoff: The Space you used last is no longer moved next to the current one.

name: Group windows by app in Mission Control
summary: Mission Control stacks each app's windows together.
benefit: With many windows open, the right one is easier to find in Mission Control.
tradeoff: Windows are shown smaller and partly overlap each other.

name: Tiled windows without gaps
summary: Windows snapped to halves or quarters fill the screen edge to edge.
benefit: More room for content when two or four windows are tiled.
tradeoff: No visual separation between tiled windows.

name: Stage Manager is off
summary: Shows whether Stage Manager is on. Keel only reads this setting.
benefit: Windows stay where you put them, with no thumbnail strip at the screen edge.
tradeoff: You lose Stage Manager's window sets if you used them.

name: Move windows by dragging anywhere
summary: Hold Control and Command and drag any part of a window to move it.
benefit: Windows can be moved from any point, including apps with no visible title bar.
tradeoff: Control-Command-drag inside a window no longer reaches the app itself, which few apps use.

name: Window open animation: off
summary: New windows and sheets appear at once instead of zooming in.
benefit: Windows and dialogs appear as soon as you open them.
tradeoff: Less visual cue about where a new window came from.

name: Instant sheet and zoom resizing
summary: Windows that resize themselves do so in 1 ms instead of about 200 ms.
benefit: Settings windows and sheets change size without animating.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Title bar document icon without delay
summary: Hovering a window title shows the document icon immediately instead of after a pause.
benefit: The document icon is ready to drag or Command-click as soon as you point at the title.
tradeoff: Title bars show the icon whenever the pointer passes over them.

name: Finder animations: off
summary: Get Info windows and some Finder zooms appear without animation.
benefit: Finder info windows open without the zoom.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Quick Look zoom animation: off
summary: Space-bar previews skip the zoom animation, mainly when closing.
benefit: Previews close slightly faster.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Wallpaper tinting in windows: off
summary: Window backgrounds stop picking up a color tint from the wallpaper.
benefit: Neutral window backgrounds regardless of the wallpaper.
tradeoff: Windows look slightly less integrated with the desktop.

name: Reduce transparency
summary: Blurred, translucent panels become solid. Keel opens the setting for you.
benefit: Flat, higher-contrast panels that are easier to read; possibly slightly less graphics work.
tradeoff: The translucent look is gone and panels look flatter.

name: Reduce motion
summary: Space switches and Mission Control fade instead of sliding and zooming.
benefit: Calmer transitions between Spaces and full-screen apps.
tradeoff: Some transitions lose their sense of direction.

name: Fixed 60 Hz instead of ProMotion
summary: Caps a ProMotion display at 60 Hz. Small battery gain, less smooth motion.
benefit: Slightly longer battery life when a lot moves on screen.
tradeoff: Scrolling and animations are visibly less smooth.

name: Electron apps include the WindowServer fix
summary: Checks each Electron app for the release that fixed constant window-shadow redraws.
benefit: If an outdated app was the cause, WindowServer CPU use and lag drop once it is updated.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: No High Power Mode on battery
summary: On battery the Mac uses Automatic instead of High Power, which mainly runs the fans harder.
benefit: Quieter fans and somewhat longer battery life when unplugged. Everyday work runs the same.
tradeoff: Heavy jobs that run on battery for longer than about 15 minutes may finish somewhat later.
cmds: sudo pmset -b powermode 0   # lowpowermode on Macs without High Power Mode

name: High Power Mode on the power adapter
summary: While plugged in, the fans may run faster so long renders, builds and model runs throttle less.
benefit: Renders, exports, builds and model runs longer than 10–15 minutes may slow down less as the Mac heats up.
tradeoff: Louder fans under load and slightly higher power draw. Short tasks are not faster.
cmds: sudo pmset -c powermode 2   # lowpowermode on Macs without High Power Mode

name: No Low Power Mode on the power adapter
summary: While plugged in, the Mac uses Automatic instead of Low Power Mode, so CPU and GPU speed are not capped.
benefit: Heavy work while plugged in runs at full speed again instead of being capped.
tradeoff: More heat and fan noise under load than with Low Power Mode.
cmds: sudo pmset -c powermode 0   # lowpowermode on Macs without High Power Mode

name: Low Power Mode on battery
summary: The Mac uses Low Power Mode whenever it is unplugged, for longer battery life and slower heavy work.
benefit: The battery lasts longer, most of all during heavy work, and the Mac runs cooler and quieter unplugged.
tradeoff: Builds, exports and games run much slower on battery.
cmds: sudo pmset -b powermode 1   # lowpowermode on Macs without High Power Mode

name: Nothing is keeping the Mac awake
summary: Lists apps that are stopping the Mac from sleeping right now, such as a forgotten call or video tab.
benefit: You see why the Mac did not sleep or why the battery drained overnight, and which app to quit.
tradeoff: Nothing. Keel only reads the current state.

name: Sleep when idle on battery
summary: On battery, the Mac and its display go to sleep when idle instead of staying on indefinitely.
benefit: An open, unused Mac on battery goes to sleep instead of running flat.
tradeoff: Unattended work that does not ask macOS to stay awake pauses when the Mac sleeps on battery.
cmds: sudo pmset -b displaysleep 10   # only if it is 0
sudo pmset -b sleep 1   # only if it is 0

name: Stay awake on the power adapter
summary: While plugged in, the display still turns off but the Mac keeps running jobs, servers and downloads.
benefit: Long jobs, servers and downloads keep running overnight while the Mac is plugged in.
tradeoff: The Mac uses more power when idle on the power adapter, because it never sleeps on its own.

name: Power Nap off on battery
summary: The Mac no longer wakes briefly while asleep on battery to fetch Mail and sync iCloud.
benefit: Slightly less battery used overnight while the lid is closed.
tradeoff: Mail, Calendar and iCloud are not refreshed while the Mac sleeps on battery.

name: TCP keep-alive off on battery
summary: Fewer wakes while asleep on battery, but no push notifications or Find My location during sleep.
benefit: Slightly less battery used while the Mac sleeps on battery.
tradeoff: No notifications, Messages or Find My location while the Mac sleeps on battery.

name: Wake for network access off
summary: Other devices can no longer wake this Mac over the network for file sharing or Screen Sharing.
benefit: The Mac stays asleep instead of waking for network traffic.
tradeoff: Remote access to the sleeping Mac (file sharing, Screen Sharing, SSH) stops working.

name: Network wake only on the power adapter
summary: Keeps remote wake while plugged in, but network requests no longer wake the Mac on battery.
benefit: A sleeping Mac on battery is no longer woken by network requests.
tradeoff: On battery, you cannot reach the sleeping Mac remotely.

name: Slightly dim the display on battery
summary: The display dims slightly on battery and returns to its normal brightness when plugged in.
benefit: A little more battery time during light use.
tradeoff: The screen is a little darker when unplugged.

name: Optimize video streaming on battery
summary: On battery, streamed HDR video plays in standard range to save energy. Only System Settings can set it.
benefit: Longer battery life while watching HDR shows and videos unplugged.
tradeoff: HDR video looks less vivid on battery.

name: Safe sleep settings (Apple defaults)
summary: The Mac keeps saving a copy of open work to disk when it sleeps, as Apple ships it.
benefit: Open work survives a completely drained battery, and long sleeps use less battery.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable on the defaults. It undoes hibernatemode 25 if you set that for security.
cmds: sudo pmset -b|-c hibernatemode 3   # only where it differs
sudo pmset -b|-c standby 1   # only where it differs

name: Start up after a power failure
summary: A desktop Mac starts up again on its own when power returns after an outage.
benefit: After an outage the Mac comes back online without anyone pressing the power button.
tradeoff: The Mac also starts up when power returns at times you wanted it to stay off.

name: Remove the repeating power schedule
summary: Removes a weekly scheduled restart, shutdown, sleep or wake, after recording it so it can be put back.
benefit: Overnight work is no longer cut off by a scheduled restart or shutdown.
tradeoff: The scheduled event no longer happens.

name: Battery health
summary: Shows the battery's cycle count and remaining capacity compared with when it was new.
benefit: You know whether a short battery life comes from a worn battery rather than from settings.
tradeoff: Nothing. Keel only reads the current state.

name: Battery charge limit
summary: Holds the battery below 100 % on a Mac that is mostly plugged in. Only System Settings can set it.
benefit: The battery keeps more of its capacity over the years if the Mac is mostly plugged in.
tradeoff: Less charge is available when you unplug unexpectedly.

name: Not slowed down by heat
summary: Checks whether macOS is currently lowering speed because the Mac is too hot.
benefit: You learn whether heat is why the Mac feels slow.
tradeoff: Nothing. Keel only reads the current state.

name: Metal Performance HUD in all apps
summary: Shows Apple's frame-rate and GPU overlay in every Metal app and game you open next.
benefit: Games and 3D apps show live frame rate and GPU timing in a corner overlay.
tradeoff: The overlay covers part of the window in every Metal app until you turn it off.

name: Force Game Mode on (experimental)
summary: Keeps Game Mode on all the time instead of only while a full-screen game runs. Needs Xcode.
benefit: Windowed games may get Game Mode's priority and lower controller and AirPods latency. Other work is not faster.
tradeoff: Background apps get lower priority while it is forced on.

name: AirDrop receiving: No One
summary: Other people's devices can no longer find this Mac in AirDrop. You can still send files.
benefit: Fewer AWDL wake-ups from nearby devices, one of the causes of short lag spikes on Wi-Fi. Strangers cannot send you AirDrop requests.
tradeoff: Nobody can AirDrop to this Mac until you choose Contacts Only or Everyone in Control Center.

name: Handoff and Universal Clipboard off
summary: This Mac stops sharing open activities and the clipboard with your iPhone and iPad.
benefit: The Handoff icon no longer appears in the Dock for activities from your phone, and sharingd stops advertising this Mac's activity.
tradeoff: No Handoff between devices and no copy on iPhone, paste on Mac.

name: AirPlay Receiver off
summary: Other devices can no longer cast to this Mac, and it stops listening on ports 5000 and 7000.
benefit: This Mac disappears from other devices' AirPlay menus and has two fewer open network ports.
tradeoff: You cannot mirror an iPhone or another Mac to this screen.

name: AWDL off for this session
summary: Turns off the device-to-device Wi-Fi link until the Mac sleeps, removing its lag spikes.
benefit: Steadier ping on Wi-Fi in games, calls and remote desktop until the Mac next sleeps.
tradeoff: AirDrop, AirPlay, Sidecar, Universal Control, Continuity Camera and Auto Unlock with Apple Watch stop working until awdl0 is back up.

name: DNS: Cloudflare, current resolver as fallback
summary: The active network service looks up names with 1.1.1.1. Run the Benchmark DNS test first.
benefit: Pages on sites you have not visited recently can start loading a little sooner, about 30 ms per lookup on the network where it was measured.
tradeoff: Names only your router knows may stop resolving, and office or hotel networks that rely on their own DNS can misbehave on this service.
cmds: sudo networksetup -setdnsservers <active service> 1.1.1.1 1.0.0.1 <current resolvers or router>

name: Content Caching for your other Apple devices
summary: This Mac keeps local copies of Apple updates and apps for the other Apple devices on your network.
benefit: Updates and app downloads on your other Apple devices finish at home-network speed and come over the internet once.
tradeoff: Uses disk space on this Mac (you can set a limit) and only serves devices while this Mac is awake.

name: Bonjour advertising off
summary: This Mac stops announcing its name and services on the local network. Applies after a restart.
benefit: After a restart, this Mac's name and services no longer appear to other people on the same network.
tradeoff: Nobody can AirDrop to it over the local network, AirPlay to it, or find its shared folders, screen or printers by name.

name: Thunderbolt Bridge service off
summary: Turns off the unused Mac-to-Mac Thunderbolt network service. Tidier, not faster.
benefit: One fewer entry in Network settings. No measurable speed change.
tradeoff: Migration Assistant over a cable, Share Disk and Mac-to-Mac clustering need it turned back on.

name: iCloud Private Relay
summary: Shows a hint of the relay's state and opens its setting. macOS has no supported way to read it.
benefit: You can compare networkQuality with and without the relay and decide per network.
tradeoff: With the relay off, websites and trackers in Safari and Mail see your IP address.

name: Google Updater background agent
summary: Chrome's updater stops waking up every hour. Chrome still checks for updates when you open it.
benefit: One fewer job waking the Mac every hour. Nothing changes on screen.
tradeoff: Chrome updates only while it is open, and Google apps you rarely open stay on older versions until you do.

name: Zoom updater agents
summary: Zoom stops checking for updates at login and twice a day. Update from the app instead.
benefit: No update check at login and no scheduled update runs.
tradeoff: Zoom updates only when you choose Check for Updates in the app, which asks for an administrator password.

name: Zoom privileged helper
summary: Removes the helper Zoom keeps installed, with root rights, for updates. Less to attack, not less CPU use.
benefit: One fewer service running as root; meetings work as before.
tradeoff: In-app updates fail with error 10008 until Zoom re-installs the helper, which asks for an administrator password.

name: SteelSeries GG at login
summary: The SteelSeries GG app no longer opens by itself at login.
benefit: One fewer Electron app at login; apps of this kind usually run several processes and use hundreds of MB.
tradeoff: Settings that GG applies (EQ, lighting, macros) are not applied until you open GG. Settings stored on the device keep working.

name: BlueStacks clean-up daemon
summary: Removes a BlueStacks job that runs as root and watches /Applications/BlueStacks.app.
benefit: One fewer root job, and the "now.gg, Inc." row leaves Login Items & Extensions.
tradeoff: If BlueStacks.app is installed, its clean-up after an uninstall does not run.

name: Review Login Items & Extensions
summary: Lists the third-party jobs macOS starts in the background and which ones Keel has a card for.
benefit: A list of what starts in the background, with a pointer to the card for each item Keel can turn off.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable: Keel only reads these folders.

name: Don't reopen apps after a restart
summary: The restart dialog starts with "Reopen windows when logging back in" turned off.
benefit: After a restart only your login items open, so the Mac is ready sooner and forgotten apps stay closed.
tradeoff: Open apps and windows are not restored after a restart unless you select the checkbox in the dialog.

name: Spotify at login
summary: Spotify opens itself at every login unless this is turned off in Spotify's settings.
benefit: Spotify no longer appears after you log in.
tradeoff: Open Spotify yourself when you want it.

name: Show build duration in Xcode
summary: Each build's duration appears in Xcode's activity area, so build changes can be measured.
benefit: Every build shows how many seconds it took, so you can tell whether a change made builds faster or slower.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Xcode indexing progress as numbers
summary: Xcode shows how many files it has indexed out of the total, instead of only a progress bar.
benefit: While a project indexes, the activity area shows a rising file count, so you can see how much is left.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Xcode: compile on the 10 performance cores
summary: Xcode compiles at most as many files at once as the Mac has performance cores.
benefit: During big builds the rest of the Mac (scrolling, the simulator, your browser) stays responsive.
tradeoff: Very large clean builds can take slightly longer because the efficiency cores no longer compile.

name: Xcode on-device code predictions: off
summary: Xcode stops loading its local machine-learning model for gray whole-line code suggestions.
benefit: Xcode no longer loads the prediction model, which leaves more memory for simulators and builds. The amount saved was not measured.
tradeoff: No gray whole-line suggestions while you type, and String Catalogs can no longer generate translator comments, which need the same model.

name: Git: built-in file monitor and untracked cache
summary: git status asks macOS what changed instead of rescanning every file; large repositories gain most.
benefit: git status, diff and add return sooner in large repositories, and editors that run git status in the background wait less.
tradeoff: One small background fsmonitor daemon per repository you work in, until you log out.

name: SSH: reuse connections for 10 minutes
summary: git push/pull and ssh to the same server skip the connection handshake after the first time.
benefit: The second and later git push, pull or ssh to the same server within 10 minutes start without the usual connection delay, most visibly over slow or distant links.
tradeoff: After a network change the first command may hang until the old connection times out (`ssh -O exit <host>` closes it at once); a shared connection stays open in the background for 10 minutes.
cmds:
append to ~/.ssh/config:
# >>> Keel: reuse SSH connections (remove this block or restore in Keel to undo) >>>
Host *
    ControlMaster auto
    ControlPath ~/.ssh/keel-cm-%C
    ControlPersist 10m
# <<< Keel <<<

name: Terminal as a Developer Tool
summary: Programs you build and run from Terminal skip macOS's security check on first launch.
benefit: Freshly built binaries and test executables start without the first-launch pause. The size of the pause was not measured by Keel.
tradeoff: Anything started from that terminal, including a downloaded script or binary, runs without Gatekeeper's malware check. Use it only for terminals you use for your own code.

name: Crash reports as notifications, not dialogs
summary: "App quit unexpectedly" appears as a notification instead of a window you must dismiss.
benefit: When an app crashes, a notification slides in and your current window keeps focus.
tradeoff: Crash messages are easier to miss if you have notifications silenced.

name: Keep straight quotes and double hyphens
summary: macOS no longer turns " into “ ” and -- into — in Notes, Mail, Messages and other Mac apps.
benefit: Shell commands and code written in Notes, Mail or Messages keep plain " ' and -- and paste into a terminal unchanged.
tradeoff: Prose in Mac apps gets straight quotes and hyphens instead of typographic ones.

name: Homebrew: no analytics
summary: Homebrew stops sending anonymous install and usage events.
benefit: Nothing changes on screen; brew stops sending analytics.
tradeoff: Homebrew's maintainers get less data on which packages are used.

name: No .DS_Store files on network shares
summary: Finder no longer leaves .DS_Store files in folders on file servers and NAS shares.
benefit: No stray .DS_Store files appear on file servers, NAS shares or in colleagues' folders, and browsing big network folders is slightly quicker.
tradeoff: Finder does not remember icon positions or view options for folders on network shares.

name: Docker: Resource Saver after 2 minutes idle
summary: Docker pauses its Linux VM after 2 minutes without running containers, instead of 5.
benefit: After you stop your containers, Docker's memory (2 GB or more, per Docker) is returned 3 minutes sooner.
tradeoff: The first docker command after a pause waits 3 to 10 seconds while the VM resumes.
cmds: settings-store.json: UseResourceSaver = true, AutoPauseTimeoutSeconds = 120  (Docker Desktop must be quit)

name: Docker: cap the VM to fit your Mac
summary: Keeps container builds from starving Xcode, the simulator and the rest of the Mac.
benefit: While containers run, Docker can take at most 8 GB and 7 cores, so Xcode, browsers and simulators stay responsive (the default allows 12 GB).
tradeoff: Memory-hungry container stacks can hit the VM's limit, and containers that run out of memory are stopped (OOM-killed); builds inside Docker use fewer cores.
cmds: settings-store.json: Cpus = 7, MemoryMiB = 8192  (Docker Desktop must be quit)

name: Docker: no start at login, no dashboard
summary: Docker Desktop starts only when you open it, without the dashboard window.
benefit: Docker's virtual machine is not running after login, so its memory stays free until you open Docker.
tradeoff: Open Docker Desktop before running docker commands.
cmds: settings-store.json: AutoStart = false, OpenUIOnStartupDisabled = true  (Docker Desktop must be quit)

name: Docker: don't send usage statistics
summary: Turns off Docker Desktop's "Send usage statistics", which is on by default.
benefit: Nothing visible; Docker Desktop stops sending usage data.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.
cmds: settings-store.json: AnalyticsEnabled = false  (Docker Desktop must be quit)

name: Spotlight: stop indexing code dependencies
summary: Shows which code folders Spotlight indexes, including node_modules, and how to exclude them.
benefit: Less Spotlight indexing activity (mds_stores) after every npm/pnpm/yarn install or build, and Spotlight results without thousands of dependency files.
tradeoff: Files in excluded folders are not found by Spotlight or Finder search.

name: GPU memory for local AI, sized for your Mac
summary: Lets Ollama, LM Studio and MLX keep up to 20 GiB of a model on the GPU, leaving 4 GiB to macOS.
benefit: About 2.24 GiB more room for models on the GPU. A model that was split between CPU and GPU loads fully on the GPU and can generate several times faster; models that already fit run the same.
tradeoff: While a large model is loaded, only 4 GiB is left for macOS and your apps; with many apps open the Mac starts to swap.
cmds: sudo sysctl -w iogpu.wired_limit_mb=<sized for your Mac>
sudo launchctl bootout system/com.keel.iogpu-wired-limit; sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.keel.iogpu-wired-limit.plist  # only if Keel v1's daemon exists
sudo install /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.keel.sysctl.iogpu-wired_limit_mb.plist  # runs sysctl -w iogpu.wired_limit_mb=<sized for your Mac> at boot
brew services restart ollama / reopen Ollama.app  # only if running

name: Ollama: flash attention + q8_0 KV cache
summary: Halves the memory Ollama needs for a conversation's context. Homebrew's service already sets both.
benefit: Longer conversations or a larger model fit in memory, because the context cache takes half the space.
tradeoff: A very small loss of precision in the cache. Nothing noticeable in normal use.
cmds: brew services restart ollama  # only if the service is loaded
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION 1  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE q8_0  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
quit and reopen Ollama.app if it is open

name: Ollama: default context sized for your memory
summary: Ollama reads up to 16384 tokens by default instead of 4096, so long prompts are no longer cut without warning.
benefit: Long prompts, files and chat histories up to 16384 tokens are no longer cut off without warning.
tradeoff: Each loaded model uses more memory for its context, about 1 GB for an 8B model at 16K with the 8-bit cache.
cmds: brew services restart ollama  # only if the service is loaded
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH 16384  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
quit and reopen Ollama.app if it is open

name: Ollama: keep model loaded 30 min
summary: Ollama keeps the last model loaded for 30 minutes instead of 5, so the next prompt does not wait for a reload.
benefit: No loading pause when your prompts are less than 30 minutes apart.
tradeoff: The model's memory stays in use for 30 minutes after you stop using it.
cmds: brew services restart ollama  # only if the service is loaded
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE 30m  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
quit and reopen Ollama.app if it is open

name: Ollama: keep 1 GiB of the GPU budget free
summary: After the GPU memory limit is raised, Ollama leaves its last GiB free when deciding how much of a model fits.
benefit: The Mac stays responsive when a model nearly fills the raised GPU limit.
tradeoff: Ollama plans with 1 GiB less, so a model that barely fit may run partly on the CPU.
cmds: brew services restart ollama  # only if the service is loaded
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD 1073741824  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
quit and reopen Ollama.app if it is open

name: Ollama: one model in memory at a time
summary: Ollama holds one model in memory instead of up to 3, so switching models frees memory at once.
benefit: Switching models frees the old model's memory immediately instead of minutes later.
tradeoff: Tools that use two models together (embeddings plus chat) reload a model on every switch.
cmds: brew services restart ollama  # only if the service is loaded
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS 1  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
quit and reopen Ollama.app if it is open

name: Ollama: reachable only from this Mac
summary: Ollama accepts connections only from this Mac. It has no password, so on the network anyone could use your models.
benefit: Other devices on your network can no longer use or change your local models.
tradeoff: Using Ollama from another device, such as a phone or a second computer, stops working.
cmds: brew services restart ollama  # only if the service is loaded
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST 127.0.0.1:11434  # Ollama.app; login agent com.keel.ollama-env repeats it
quit and reopen Ollama.app if it is open

name: Ollama: local only, no cloud models
summary: Ollama refuses its cloud models and web search on ollama.com, so every prompt stays on this Mac.
benefit: Nothing you type into Ollama is sent to ollama.com, even by a tool that picks a cloud model.
tradeoff: Cloud models and Ollama's web search stop working.
cmds: restart Ollama if it is running

name: Ollama service: start it only when needed
summary: Homebrew's Ollama service no longer starts at login or restarts itself; start it when you need it.
benefit: No Ollama server runs in the background when you are not using local models.
tradeoff: Apps that call Ollama at localhost:11434 fail until you run `brew services start ollama`.

name: LM Studio load settings for this Mac
summary: Lists the LM Studio load settings that suit this Mac: full GPU offload, flash attention, 8-bit cache, context size.
benefit: Models run entirely on the GPU and their context takes half the memory, so larger models and longer chats fit.
tradeoff: The 8-bit cache loses a very small amount of precision. Nothing noticeable in normal use.

name: llama.cpp server: 8-bit KV cache
summary: llama-server keeps conversation context in 16-bit by default. Two options halve that memory.
benefit: The same model fits a context about twice as long, or leaves more memory for other apps.
tradeoff: A very small loss of precision in the cache. Nothing noticeable in normal use.

name: Keep large local models on an external SSD
summary: Local models can take tens of GB of the internal disk. Ollama, LM Studio and MLX can load them from an SSD.
benefit: Frees the internal disk space your models use, often tens of gigabytes.
tradeoff: Models are available only while the drive is connected, and they load as fast as the drive reads.

name: Shut down background iOS simulators
summary: Simulators left running after you quit Simulator or Xcode are shut down, and their memory is freed.
benefit: The memory held by forgotten simulators, shown in the details, becomes available to other apps.
tradeoff: The next simulator or preview launch is a cold boot and takes a few seconds longer.
cmds: xcrun simctl shutdown all   # only while Simulator.app is closed
xcrun simctl --set previews shutdown all   # only while Xcode is closed

name: Memory pressure is normal
summary: Checks whether the Mac is actually short of memory. A high "memory used" figure on its own is normal.
benefit: You see whether memory is really what slows the Mac down, and which apps use the most.
tradeoff: Nothing. Keel only reads the current state.

name: Chrome, Brave, Chromium: Memory Saver
summary: Google Chrome unloads tabs you have not used for a while and reloads them when you return. Quit Google Chrome first.
benefit: With many tabs open, the browser holds less memory. How much depends on how many tabs sit unused.
tradeoff: Old tabs reload when you switch back to them, and unsaved text typed into them can be lost.
cmds: Google Chrome quit; Local State: performance_tuning.high_efficiency_mode.state = 2, aggressiveness kept (1 = Balanced if unset)

name: Chrome, Brave, Chromium: Energy Saver on battery
summary: Google Chrome limits background activity whenever the Mac is on battery, not only below 20 %. Quit Google Chrome first.
benefit: The browser uses less CPU on battery, which helps battery life most with many tabs open.
tradeoff: On battery, background tabs update less often and some animations and video run at a lower frame rate.

name: Chrome, Brave, Chromium: hardware acceleration stays on
summary: Checks that Google Chrome still draws pages and video with the GPU rather than the CPU.
benefit: You find out if an old troubleshooting step left the browser drawing on the CPU.
tradeoff: Nothing. Keel only reads the current state.

name: At least 15 % of the disk is free
summary: Checks that the startup disk has real free space, not only space macOS might purge later.
benefit: A warning before low space makes updates fail, apps stall while saving, or swap run out.
tradeoff: Nothing; Keel only reads the numbers.

name: Release space held by local snapshots
summary: Frees space that Time Machine local snapshots still hold after files are deleted.
benefit: Space you already deleted shows up as free again, often many GB right after a big cleanup or update.
tradeoff: The hourly on-device restore points for the last day are gone; Time Machine starts taking new ones within the hour.

name: Time Machine: skip developer caches
summary: Keeps build output, simulators and package caches out of Time Machine backups.
benefit: Smaller, faster hourly backups and more backup history kept on the same drive.
tradeoff: After a restore from backup, these caches are rebuilt or downloaded again on first use.
cmds: tmutil addexclusion <each listed folder that is still included>

name: Time Machine: skip virtual machine disks
summary: Keeps UTM, Parallels, VMware, OrbStack, Docker and other VM images out of backups.
benefit: Hourly backups stop copying whole VM disks, so they finish sooner and the backup drive holds more history.
tradeoff: VMs are not in Time Machine; restoring the Mac from backup will not bring them back.
cmds: sudo tmutil addexclusion -p <each listed VM folder>

name: Time Machine backup at full disk speed
summary: Turns off background disk throttling until restart, for a first or overdue backup.
benefit: A large backup finishes sooner; in the one published test it took about 60 % as long.
tradeoff: While it is on, apps can pause when Spotlight, iCloud or the backup use the disk heavily. Turn it off or restart when the backup is done.

name: Time Machine new-disk prompt: off
summary: Connecting a new drive no longer asks whether to use it for Time Machine backups.
benefit: No dialog each time a USB drive or SD card is connected.
tradeoff: Time Machine no longer suggests new backup disks; set one up in System Settings when you want one.

name: iCloud “Optimize Mac Storage” status
summary: Shows whether iCloud Drive may remove local copies of files. Keel only reads it.
benefit: You can see whether every iCloud Drive file is on this Mac and in your backups.
tradeoff: Nothing; Keel only reads it.

name: Empty Trash items older than 30 days
summary: Finder permanently deletes items that have been in the Trash for 30 days.
benefit: The Trash no longer grows to many GB unnoticed.
tradeoff: Anything left in the Trash for 30 days is deleted permanently.

name: Apple personalized ads off
summary: App Store, Apple News and Stocks stop choosing ads from your account information.
benefit: Ads in Apple's apps no longer reflect your account's interest segments.
tradeoff: Those ads become less relevant to you.

name: Mac and app analytics off
summary: The Mac stops sending crash and usage reports to Apple and to app developers.
benefit: No diagnostic or usage reports leave the Mac automatically.
tradeoff: Apple and app developers get no crash reports from you to fix bugs with.

name: Siri and Dictation recordings: not shared
summary: Apple does not keep your Siri and Dictation audio for review by staff.
benefit: Your voice requests are not stored for human grading.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.
cmds: defaults write com.apple.assistant.support 'Siri Data Sharing Opt-In Status' -int 2

name: Look Up suggestions off
summary: Look Up stops sending the word you clicked to Apple for web and Siri Knowledge results.
benefit: Words you look up stay on the Mac.
tradeoff: No web or Siri Knowledge results in the Look Up panel.

name: Spotlight: Siri Suggestions off
summary: Spotlight stops sending what you type to Apple. Keel opens the setting; it cannot read it.
benefit: Spotlight searches stay on the Mac.
tradeoff: No web, Wikipedia or Siri suggestions in Spotlight results.

name: Location: Significant Locations off
summary: The Mac stops keeping a history of places you visit. Keel opens the setting; it cannot read it.
benefit: No record of places you visit is kept on the Mac.
tradeoff: Fewer location-aware suggestions in Maps, Calendar and Siri.

name: Notification previews hidden on lock screen
summary: Message text stays hidden while the Mac is locked. Keel checks the setting and opens it.
benefit: Someone looking at your locked Mac sees who wrote, not what they wrote.
tradeoff: You sign in to the Mac to read a notification's text.

name: Terminal: Secure Keyboard Entry
summary: Other apps cannot read what you type in Terminal, including sudo and ssh passwords.
benefit: Passwords typed in Terminal are out of reach of other apps.
tradeoff: While Terminal is in front, text expanders and global keyboard tools cannot see your typing.

name: Firewall on, stealth mode on
summary: Blocks unrequested incoming connections and stops the Mac answering scans. No speed cost.
benefit: On public networks nothing can connect to this Mac unasked, and it does not answer network scans.
tradeoff: Apps that accept connections ask once to be allowed, and the Mac no longer answers ping.
cmds: sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on   # skipped if already on or set to block all

name: Guest user off
summary: Removes the Guest User from the login window.
benefit: Nobody can log in to this Mac without an account of their own.
tradeoff: No guest session for visitors or for someone returning a lost Mac.

name: Login window asks for name and password
summary: The login window shows empty name and password fields instead of a list of users.
benefit: After you log out, the login window no longer shows account names and pictures.
tradeoff: You type your account name as well as your password at that window.

name: Sharing services off when unused
summary: Lists the Sharing services that let other computers reach this Mac. Keel only reads them.
benefit: You see at a glance which ways into this Mac are open on the network.
tradeoff: Services you turn off can no longer be reached from other computers.

name: Password right after sleep or screen saver
summary: Checks that the Mac asks for a password within 5 seconds of the display sleeping. Keel opens the setting.
benefit: Letting the display sleep locks the Mac at once.
tradeoff: You authenticate (password, Touch ID or Apple Watch) every time the display wakes.

name: Automatic login off
summary: Checks that the Mac asks for a password at startup instead of logging in by itself.
benefit: Nobody reaches your files by turning the Mac on.
tradeoff: You type your password at startup.

name: Allow accessories to connect: ask
summary: New USB and Thunderbolt devices need your approval before they can reach your data.
benefit: A charging station or unknown cable cannot read from or talk to the Mac without your approval.
tradeoff: With Always Ask, you approve your own docks and drives each time you connect them.

name: FileVault on
summary: Checks that the data on the disk can only be read with your password.
benefit: Data on a lost or stolen Mac cannot be read without your password.
tradeoff: If you lose both your password and the recovery key, the data cannot be recovered.

name: System Integrity Protection on
summary: Checks that System Integrity Protection is on. Turning it off never speeds anything up.
benefit: Malware cannot modify the operating system, even with your password.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Gatekeeper on
summary: Checks that apps must be signed and notarized by Apple before they open.
benefit: Unsigned or tampered apps are stopped before they run.
tradeoff: Unsigned apps need a one-time approval in Privacy & Security.

name: Security responses and system files: on
summary: Checks that urgent security fixes and malware definitions install by themselves.
benefit: Malware definitions and urgent fixes arrive within hours instead of with the next macOS release.
tradeoff: An urgent fix can occasionally ask for a restart.

name: Lockdown Mode
summary: Shows whether Lockdown Mode is on. It is meant for people at risk of targeted attacks.
benefit: For people at risk of targeted attacks, a much smaller attack surface.
tradeoff: Many attachments, link previews, web fonts and some websites stop working.

name: Chromium-based browsers: URL sharing off
summary: The browser stops sending the addresses you visit to its maker. Quit the browser first.
benefit: Visited addresses are no longer sent to Google or Microsoft for suggestions.
tradeoff: Address-bar suggestions are slightly less tailored.
cmds: Each profile's Preferences: url_keyed_anonymized_data_collection.enabled = false  (browser quit; file copied to backups first)

name: Chromium-based browsers: Standard Safe Browsing
summary: Keeps malicious-site protection without real-time upload of visited addresses. Quit the browser first.
benefit: Addresses you visit and files you download are no longer sent to Google for real-time checks.
tradeoff: Slower protection against brand-new phishing and malware sites than Enhanced protection.
cmds: Each profile's Preferences: safebrowsing.enhanced = false  (browser quit; file copied to backups first)

name: Chromium-based browsers: usage statistics off
summary: The browser stops uploading usage statistics and crash reports. Quit the browser first.
benefit: No usage statistics or crash reports leave the browser.
tradeoff: The browser maker gets no crash data from you.
cmds: Each profile's Local State: user_experience_metrics.reporting_enabled = false  (browser quit; file copied to backups first)

name: Intel-only apps and Rosetta
summary: Lists apps and running processes that still need Rosetta, Apple's Intel translator.
benefit: Knowing which apps run slower and will stop working once Rosetta is gone.
tradeoff: Nothing: this only reports.

name: Show all filename extensions
summary: Finder shows the full name of every file, including .pdf, .app or .zip at the end.
benefit: You can see what kind of file something is, and spot files disguised with a double extension.
tradeoff: File names are slightly longer in Finder and Open dialogs.

name: Finder path bar and status bar
summary: Finder windows show the folder path at the bottom, plus item count and free space.
benefit: You always see which folder you are in and how much disk space is left.
tradeoff: Finder windows lose about two lines of height for file listings.

name: New Finder windows open your home folder
summary: New Finder windows open your home folder instead of Recents.
benefit: Each new Finder window opens at the same predictable place, without waiting for a Recents search.
tradeoff: Recently used files are one click away in the sidebar instead of shown first.

name: Finder searches the current folder
summary: Searching from a Finder window looks in that folder instead of the whole Mac.
benefit: Searching inside a project or Downloads folder lists only matches from that folder.
tradeoff: To search the whole Mac from a Finder window, click “This Mac” in the search bar.

name: Folders on top when sorting by name
summary: Finder lists folders before files when a window is sorted by name.
benefit: Folders are always at the top of the list.
tradeoff: Nothing noticeable.

name: Extension change warning: off
summary: Renaming a file's extension no longer asks for confirmation.
benefit: Renaming files between formats takes one step instead of two.
tradeoff: No safety prompt if you change an extension by mistake; the file may then open in the wrong app.

name: Full folder path in Finder title bars
summary: Finder window titles show the full path, such as /Users/you/Projects/app.
benefit: You can tell folders with the same name apart, and match Finder windows to Terminal paths.
tradeoff: Long paths make window titles crowded.

name: Show the Library folder in your home
summary: Your ~/Library folder becomes visible in Finder.
benefit: ~/Library is visible in your home folder like any other folder.
tradeoff: Files that apps depend on are easier to move or delete by mistake.
cmds: clear the invisible bit in the com.apple.FinderInfo attribute of ~/Library

name: Show hidden files in Finder
summary: Finder shows files and folders whose names start with a dot, dimmed.
benefit: Configuration files are visible in Finder without a keyboard shortcut.
tradeoff: Folders show many extra files, including .DS_Store, and system files are easier to delete by mistake.

name: Save dialogs open expanded
summary: Save dialogs show the full folder browser instead of the compact pop-up.
benefit: One click fewer each time you save somewhere other than the suggested folder.
tradeoff: Save dialogs take more space on screen.

name: New documents save to this Mac by default
summary: Save dialogs for new documents suggest a folder on this Mac instead of iCloud Drive.
benefit: New files are saved to a local folder by default, not to iCloud Drive where they may later be offloaded.
tradeoff: Saving a new document to iCloud Drive takes one extra click.

name: Click wallpaper to reveal desktop: off
summary: Clicking an empty part of the desktop no longer moves every window aside.
benefit: Windows stay in place when you click the desktop by mistake.
tradeoff: To show the desktop, use Mission Control's Show Desktop (F11 or a trackpad spread) instead.

name: Widgets on the desktop: off
summary: Desktop widgets are hidden unless Stage Manager is on.
benefit: A clear desktop with no widgets behind your windows.
tradeoff: Widgets are only visible in Notification Center.

name: Screenshots go to a Screenshots folder
summary: New screenshots are saved to Pictures/Screenshots instead of piling up on the desktop.
benefit: The desktop stays clear and screenshots are in one folder.
tradeoff: Screenshots are no longer visible on the desktop right after you take them.

name: Screenshots save immediately
summary: No floating preview, so the screenshot file is written at once instead of about 5 s later.
benefit: The screenshot file exists as soon as you take it, ready to drag or attach.
tradeoff: No quick Markup from the floating preview; open the file to annotate it.

name: Window screenshots without shadow
summary: Screenshots of a single window no longer include the large drop shadow around it.
benefit: Window screenshots are cropped to the window itself.
tradeoff: Window screenshots look flat against a white page.

name: Screenshots saved as HEIC
summary: Screenshots are saved as HEIC files, which are usually smaller than PNG.
benefit: Screenshots take less disk and iCloud space and upload faster.
tradeoff: Some websites, chat tools and Windows apps cannot open HEIC; you may need to convert before sharing.

name: Faster key repeat
summary: Held keys start repeating sooner and repeat faster, at the fastest slider positions.
benefit: Moving the cursor or deleting with a held key is about three times quicker.
tradeoff: A key held slightly too long types twice until you get used to it.

name: Holding a key repeats it
summary: Held letter keys repeat instead of opening the accented-character menu.
benefit: Holding h, j, k, l or any other letter repeats it like the arrow keys do.
tradeoff: No accent menu; type accents with Option key combinations or the Character Viewer.

name: F1–F12 work as standard function keys
summary: The top row sends F1–F12 directly; hold Fn (Globe) for brightness and volume.
benefit: Keyboard shortcuts that use F-keys work with one press.
tradeoff: Brightness, volume and media keys need Fn (Globe) held.

name: Keyboard navigation between all controls
summary: Tab moves through every button and control in dialogs, not only text fields.
benefit: Dialogs such as “Don't Save / Cancel / Save” can be answered from the keyboard.
tradeoff: A focus ring appears on buttons, which some find distracting.

name: Automatic spelling correction: off
summary: macOS stops replacing words as you type; misspellings are still underlined.
benefit: What you type stays exactly as typed.
tradeoff: Real typos are no longer fixed for you; you correct them from the underline.

name: Automatic capitalization: off
summary: macOS stops capitalizing the first letter of sentences for you.
benefit: Lower-case text stays lower-case.
tradeoff: You type sentence capitals yourself.

name: Double-space inserts period: off
summary: Typing two spaces no longer turns into a period and a space.
benefit: Two spaces stay two spaces.
tradeoff: You type the period at the end of a sentence yourself.

name: Tap to click
summary: A light tap on the trackpad counts as a click, without pressing it down.
benefit: Clicking takes less pressure and is silent.
tradeoff: Resting a finger on the trackpad can cause accidental clicks while typing.

name: Three-finger drag
summary: Move windows and select text by sliding three fingers, without holding the trackpad down.
benefit: Dragging needs no pressure, which is easier on the hand for long selections.
tradeoff: Three-finger swipes between Spaces and apps move to four fingers.

name: Pointer acceleration: off (mouse)
summary: Mouse pointer movement becomes proportional to hand movement, regardless of speed.
benefit: Pointer movement is consistent, which helps aiming in games and precise design work.
tradeoff: Crossing a large screen takes more hand movement; raise Tracking speed to compensate.

name: Natural scrolling status
summary: Shows whether content follows your fingers (natural) or the scroll bar. Keel only reads it.
benefit: You can see which scroll direction is set without opening Settings.
tradeoff: Nothing; Keel only reads it.

name: Startup sound: off
summary: The Mac starts up silently instead of playing the chime.
benefit: Starting or restarting the Mac makes no sound, for example in a meeting or library.
tradeoff: No audible sign that the Mac has powered on and passed its startup checks.

name: User interface sound effects
summary: Shows whether system sounds play for actions like emptying the Trash. Keel opens the setting.
benefit: No sound effects for Finder and screenshot actions once turned off.
tradeoff: No audible confirmation that a file action or screenshot happened.

name: Volume change sound: off
summary: Pressing the volume keys no longer plays a test sound.
benefit: Adjusting volume during calls or music is silent.
tradeoff: No audible check of the new volume level.
